title: Middle Miocene climate transition
summary: Around 14 million years ago the climate took a major step toward the modern ice-house state. The East Antarctic Ice Sheet expanded rapidly and the Southern Ocean cooled and freshened in step with it. A drop in atmospheric CO2 of about 200 microatmospheres before 13.9 million years ago may have helped trigger the ice growth.

uncertainty.note: Range follows Frigola et al. (2018), "~15-13 Ma"; Leutert et al. and Raitzsch et al. both say about 14 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

when.display: c. 15–13 million years ago (centred on about 14 Ma)

where.historical_name: East Antarctica, Middle Miocene; no polities

importance.justification: A step in the long shift to the modern Antarctic ice sheet and ice-house climate.
